title: DejaVu: KV-cache Streaming for Fast, Fault-tolerant Generative LLM Serving
technique: KV-cache streaming library enabling prompt/token disaggregation in pipeline-parallel serving, microbatch swapping GPU<->CPU, and KV state replication for fault tolerance

optimized_metrics.evidence: the throughput of the disaggregated system should be maximized, and ideally be higher than the throughput of the non-disaggregated system
failures are detected and mitigated quickly to minimize recovery time
optimizes the number of machines for each stage to satisfy GPU memory capacity constraints and avoid GPU idle times

headline_claim.text: DéjàVu improves LLM serving throughput by up to 2× compared to FasterTransformer ... improve throughput by up to 1.8× ... reduces microbatch latency by 1.54× compared to non-fault-tolerant systems

reported_metrics.where: Fig 12 (median normalized latency vs request rate)
Fig 13 (req/s with/without swapping), Fig 12 sustained rate
Fig 14 cumulative latency of a microbatch under failure; Fig 15 runtime under failures

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we report normalized latency (seconds/token) for each request rate. To compute the normalized latency for each request, we divide its end-to-end latency by the number of generated tokens. Figure 12 shows the median normalized latency
metric_definitions.notes: divides by generated tokens only; median across requests; Orca/vLLM style

metric_definitions.definition_quote: First, we compute the inverse throughput (I) of the baseline.
metric_definitions.notes: analytical planner quantity used to size prompt vs token machines; derivation in §4.2.1

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Figures 20-23 show the Makespan and Normalized total cost (with respect to the hourly cost of a single VM) for various numbers of available machines for our trace.
metric_definitions.notes: simulator-based; makespan = time to finish a fixed trace; cost normalised to hourly cost of one VM

metric_definitions.definition_quote: failures are detected and mitigated quickly to minimize recovery time
metric_definitions.notes: re-pass: time to resume after a failure; reported as cumulative microbatch latency under failures

load_regime: request-rate sweep (single open-loop Poisson client, fixed 1000-token prompt, output lengths from LMSys); fixed homogeneous requests for failure experiments
tradeoff_acknowledged: Streaming/swapping add KV transfer overhead (single-batch latency slowdown, Fig 11); swapping bottlenecked by PCIe time to bring KV back; paper notes potential negative impact on throughput from differing prompt/token machine counts
hardware: A100-80GB and V100-16GB VMs (2 GPUs/stage), simulator for larger clusters
workloads: LMSys-derived output lengths, fixed prompt size 1000; homogeneous requests (500 prompt/1000 gen) for failures
extractor_notes: Throughput units not specified precisely (req/s in Fig 13). TTFT/TBT not used. Failure-recovery latency is reported as cumulative microbatch latency, not a percentile. No SLO.
load_class_quote: throughput experiments use 'a single open-loop Poisson client ... with varying request rates' (online-arrivals, txt l.~652); failure-recovery experiments use fixed homogeneous requests (offline-style)
